speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I need to evaluate a potential oncologic dermatological condition; can you describe the specific lesion you are concerned about, including its size, shape, color changes, and how quickly it has developed?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

The patient's history of heavy smoking, combined with a non-healing, crusted lesion on the penis (a high-risk site) and a similar lesion on the finger, strongly suggests cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. I will now request a biopsy of the penile lesion for histopathological confirmation.

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile lesion.
REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of left middle finger lesion.
